Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-29
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Morgan (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Amberfield CISO), Derek Cho (Amberfield Platform Engineer), Amy Tang (Amberfield Legal Ops), Noah Lim (Amberfield SRE)

Summary: see metadata - short version above
Topics: SOC2, ISO27001, SSO (SAML), RBAC, audit logs, encryption KMS, data retention policy, hosting options (hosted/dedicated/private), timeline for pilot/POC
Action items: logged in metadata

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Lena with Redwood, i think we have about 45-ish minutes, quick intros?
[00:06] Marta: Hi I'm Marta, CISO at Amberfield, thanks.
[00:09] Derek: Derek, platform team.
[00:11] Amy: Amy from legal.
[00:13] Noah: Noah SRE.
[00:15] Ravi: And I'm Ravi on infra at Redwood, happy to jump in on tech details.
[00:20] Lena: Great. The goal for today is to understand your security and deployment constraints so we can recommend Hosted, Dedicated or Private and surface any blockers. Marta, maybe you can give us the high level?
[00:30] Marta: Sure. We're evaluating LLM features across checkout, customer support bots and some supply chain queries. Main thing for us: we need strong control over keys and logs. We're SOC2 in flight, ISO could be required for certain EU partners. We already have SAML SSO via Okta and heavy RBAC controls in our own infra.
[00:52] Marta: Also data residency - EU customer data must stay in EU for some workflows. We want to avoid sending PII to third-party hosted models without encryption and access restrictions.
[01:06] Lena: Makes sense. Quick question - do you consider a Redwood hosted offering acceptable if we provide a dedicated tenancy and customer-managed KMS, or do you prefer a private deployment inside your VPC?
[01:17] Derek: short answer: for non-sensitive features hosted dedicated might be ok, but for anything touching EU PII we probably need VPC/private. Can we get a hybrid? like Dedicated in region for US and Private VPC for EU?
[01:31] Ravi: Yes we support routing by policy. You can pin EU traffic to Private or to Dedicated in an EU region depending on compliance. One detail - private on-prem vs private VPC: we have a light-weight private control plane option that installs connectors so keys never leave your KMS.
[01:48] Marta: When you say KMS never leaves, we need details. We use AWS KMS and internally HSM-backed keys for some envs. We need to ensure CMKs are customer-managed and we can audit all requests.
[01:59] Ravi: Understood. Our integration modes: 1) Hosted with Redwood-managed KMS (not ideal here), 2) Hosted with customer-managed KMS where you provide IAM roles/CMKs and we call Encrypt/Decrypt via cross-account role, 3) Private deployment where the crypto calls happen inside your VPC/air-gapped. The cross-account flow keeps keys in your account; logs of key usage live in CloudTrail on your side.
[02:22] Marta: Ok, but who signs the audit logs? We need immutable logs and we need to show them to auditors.
[02:28] Ravi: Audit logs are emitted to a customer-configurable destination. For Dedicated and Private we can push token-level trace and request/response hashes to your S3 or SIEM. For Hosted we can forward aggregated logs but some configs require dedicated tenancy to guarantee full fidelity.
[02:44] Marta: That matches my expectations. Does Redwood have SOC2 Type 2?
[02:48] Lena: Yes we have SOC2 Type 2 and an ISO27001 cert in scope for our control plane — i'll share the evidence pack. For specific deployment modes, some controls differ slightly, but the SOC2 report and mapping doc will show where responsibilities sit between Redwood and customers.
[03:04] Amy: If you could share the mapping that'd great - legal will need the shared responsibilities and data processing clauses.
[03:09] Lena: Absolutely. I'll send SOC2 report + a responsibility matrix.
[03:12] Noah: Quick practical question — key rotation and key zeroization for decommissioned models. If a key is rotated in our KMS, do cached KV caches or model artifacts still expose anything?
[03:24] Ravi: Good point. We persist only encrypted secrets in the runtime. For KV cache (the attention K/V cache), it's not stored in plaintext — it's ephemeral in memory; for Dedicated we can optionally store encrypted shards on disk but with keys from your KMS. When you rotate a key, future decrypt attempts will use the new key; we support key versioning and will maintain decryption vault entries until you purge. We can also run a re-encrypt job during maintenance window.
[03:56] Derek: there was mention of prefix caching at demo — how does caching affect data residency? If a prompt from EU is cached in a US region for performance, that's a problem.
[04:07] Ravi: Cache policy is workload-configurable. You can pin caches to region, or disable cross-region cache replication. Also ability to only cache non-PII prefixes. We also expose tagging so you can ensure EU boolean routes remain in EU.
[04:22] Marta: SSO — we use Okta with SAML and SCIM for user provisioning. We need RBAC down to model-level and route-level roles. Can Redwood integrate with SAML groups and map to RBAC?
[04:36] Lena: Yes, we integrate with SAML/SCIM and can map Okta groups to Redwood roles. For enterprise we support fine-grained RBAC, including per-route policies, model access, and billing tags.
[04:47] Marta: Any limitations? For example, can we enforce approval workflows for model rollouts?
[04:52] Ravi: We have rollout guards — approvals can be gated by groups, and you can require signed-off artifacts before promoting model variants. For Dedicated/Private you get an admin console where you can define those policies.
[05:03] Amy: From legal side, retention windows for logs is critical. We need to set retention to 7 years for audit logs for some regulated parts. Do you store raw request/response or only metadata?
[05:16] Ravi: We have multiple levels. By default we store metadata (timestamps, user, model, tokens). Raw request/response storage is an opt-in, and for Hosted it's stored encrypted with Redwood keys unless you choose customer-managed KMS or outbound to your S3. For compliance we recommend Dedicated or Private with push of raw logs to your S3/GCS with lifecycle policies you control.
[05:38] Marta: Any guarantees about immutability of logs?
[05:41] Ravi: We can sign logs and keep append-only stores in your account, or for Hosted we can timestamp and provide signed digests. For legal-grade immutability we push to your S3 with Object Lock enabled - that meets many auditors.
[05:55] Lena: There was also a question around encryption at rest and in transit — we use TLS for all in-flight. At rest it's AES-256, managed keys or customer-managed.
[06:05] Derek: Performance impact when using customer-managed KMS - we're concerned about latency for synchronous decrypt calls per request.
[06:12] Ravi: Right — that's a classic trade-off. For every token-level encryption call we'd introduce latency if we did synchronous KMS calls. Our pattern: use envelope encryption — master key in KMS unwraps a short-lived data key; the runtime caches the data key in memory per instance and rotates it periodically. That avoids per-token KMS roundtrips. For strict environments you can shorten rotation windows.
[06:35] Marta: Ok good. Can we get an architecture diagram for that flow and sample terraform IAM roles for cross-account decrypt?
[06:42] Lena: yes we'll include an architecture note and terraform snippets in the pack.
[06:46] Amy: On legal, the DPA - we want a clear statement about subprocessors and whether Redwood uses third-party clouds in a way that would cause data to cross borders.
[06:57] Lena: We use public clouds but routing is policy-driven. We can provide a subprocessor list and region mapping. For Private deployments you can run our control plane inside your VPC to avoid cross-border.
[07:08] Derek: Demo question - if we spin up a Dedicated pool in eu-west, are models pre-loaded or do we upload weights?
[07:15] Ravi: For curated models we maintain copies, but for private weights you can bring-your-own-model (BYOM). In Dedicated we can preload to reduce cold-start latency; for Private we expect you can mount your model artifacts or we can pull from your artifact registry with IAM role.
[07:30] Marta: On SOC2 mapping - we need clarity on who handles incident response if a credential leak happens. Is Redwood responsible for infra and you for config?
[07:40] Lena: It's a shared responsibility. The mapping doc will state: Redwood handles platform infra, patching, service controls; customer handles identity, their keys, and access policies. For incidents we have a joint runbook and alerting playbook — we'll share sample SLAs.
[07:56] Noah: Are you able to provide pen-test results or red team summaries?
[08:00] Lena: We can share red team/pen test executive summaries; full reports under NDA if required.
[08:06] Amy: We'll likely request the full reports under NDA.
[08:09] Lena: noted.
[08:12] Marta: A couple of gotchas — 1) we need to ensure onboarding doesn't create new cloud principals that are broad; 2) we need SSO flows for developer ops to use Redwood CLI but restrict production keys.
[08:25] Ravi: We can support least privilege roles and scoped CLI tokens. We also have short-lived service tokens that integrate with your STS.
[08:33] Derek: Cost question briefly — Dedicated adds overhead but predictable unit costs. We will want a forecast for 50 requests/s baseline with token lengths around 256 tokens average.
[08:45] Lena: We'll have Ravi run an estimate and include cost/comparison matrix for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[08:50] Amy: For procurement, timeline: legal wants vendor questionnaire answered — we'll aim to finish vetting within 3 weeks. Is that feasible?
[08:58] Lena: Yes, we'll prioritize. I will send the security pack today and Ravi will schedule the pricing session.
[09:04] Marta: One more technical: how are model rollbacks handled if we detect a quality regression? We need an ability to revert quickly and audit who approved the rollback.
[09:14] Ravi: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous model variant. Rollout approvals are logged, and audit trails include who initiated the change. Those audit entries can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[09:25] Marta: Perfect.
[09:27] Lena: ok wrapping up - recap of next steps: Lena sends SOC2 + ISO mapping + responsibility matrix + sample terraform snippets; Ravi runs latency/cost estimate and schedules dedicated pricing review with Derek; Amy will share legal redlines and request NDA for pen-test reports; Marta to confirm EU scoping for PII.
[09:44] Amy: sounds good.
[09:46] Derek: thanks everyone.
[09:47] Lena: thanks all, talk soon.
